title: Delphi Consensus on Video Laryngoscopy Readiness for Caesarean Delivery
official: Delphi Consensus on the Readiness and Availability of Video Laryngoscopy in Caesarean Delivery Settings
summary:
This study aims to develop a national expert consensus on whether video laryngoscopes should be considered essential equipment and be readily available in all clinical areas where Caesarean deliveries are performed in Canada. Video laryngoscopes are devices that help healthcare professionals see the airway during placement of a breathing tube.

The study will invite approximately 20-30 anesthesiologists from across Canada with experience in obstetric anesthesia and/or advanced airway management to complete two or three rounds of online surveys. Participants will rate statements and provide feedback on the availability of video laryngoscopes, situations in which they are important for patient safety, training expectations, and minimum equipment standards. Responses will be reviewed between rounds to identify areas of agreement and topics requiring further discussion.

The goal is to develop recommendations that can help guide clinical practice, improve preparedness for airway management during Caesarean deliveries, and support more consistent access to video laryngoscopes across Canadian healthcare settings.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Minimum of 5 years of independent clinical practice in a role involving obstetric anesthesia and/or advanced airway management.
* Current or recent (within the past 5 years) clinical practice in a Canadian healthcare setting where Caesarean deliveries are performed.
* Anesthesiologist with experience in obstetric anesthesia and/or airway management with obstetric involvement.
* Willingness to participate in all anticipated Delphi rounds (2-3 survey rounds) and to meet response timelines.
* Geographic and institutional diversity: panelists will be purposively selected to represent a range of Canadian regions and healthcare settings (academic, community, rural, varying resource levels).

Exclusion Criteria:

* Lack of current or recent (within 5 years) clinical involvement in obstetric anesthesia in a Caesarean-capable setting.
* Inability or unwillingness to complete surveys in English.
* Steering Committee members, who function as research team members and are not eligible to serve simultaneously as Delphi panelists.
